title: Atomic Habits

blink.heading: The 1% mindset
blink.body: Improvement compounds. A 1% daily gain leaves you 37x better over a year; a 1% loss leaves you near zero.

blink.heading: Identity over outcomes
blink.body: Aim to become the kind of person who does the thing, not just to achieve a result.

blink.heading: Four laws
blink.body: Make it obvious, attractive, easy, and satisfying. Invert to break bad habits.

blink.heading: Environment design
blink.body: Change your context and behaviour follows. Friction is the lever — not willpower.

insights: Habits are the compound interest of self-improvement.
Goals set direction; systems drive progress.
Your habits cast votes for the person you’re becoming.
applications: Stack a new habit onto an existing routine (habit stacking).
Make the cue visible: lay out gear, place books on the pillow.
Use a two-minute version of any habit to get started.
highlights: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
Every action is a vote for the type of person you wish to become.

flashcards.front: What are the Four Laws of Behaviour Change?
flashcards.back: Make it obvious, attractive, easy, and satisfying.
Identity goals focus on who you want to become; outcome goals focus on what you want to achieve.
